topics.title: Mass — scaled instruments: Measure and compare masses using scales; read graduated scales to measure kg and g

questions.stem: If the nine sports items are numbered from smallest mass (1) to largest mass (9), which list correctly orders the four lightest items from smallest to largest?
options: Tennis ball (58 g), table tennis bat (85 g), badminton racquet (90 g), softball bat (94 g)
Tennis ball (58 g), badminton racquet (90 g), table tennis bat (85 g), softball bat (94 g)
Table tennis bat (85 g), tennis ball (58 g), badminton racquet (90 g), softball bat (94 g)
Tennis ball (58 g), table tennis bat (85 g), softball bat (94 g), badminton racquet (90 g)
questions.hint: Find all items under 100 g (58 g, 85 g, 90 g, 94 g) and order them from smallest to largest.

keyPoints.note: Convert kg to g (1 kg = 1000 g) so every item can be compared in grams.
Compare the four items under 100 g: 58 g, 85 g, 90 g, 94 g.

steps.explain: Convert the kilogram masses to grams so all 9 items are in the same unit: \(1\text{ kg} = 1000\text{ g}\) and \(5\text{ kg} = 5000\text{ g}\).

questions.stem: When all nine sports items are numbered from smallest mass (1) to largest mass (9), which item is number 5 (the middle mass)?
questions.hint: Convert 1 kg = 1000 g and 5 kg = 5000 g, list all 9 masses from smallest to largest, and pick the 5th one.

keyPoints.note: Rank all 9 items in grams from 1 to 9.
There are 4 lighter items and 4 heavier items than the 5th item.

questions.stem: Use the sports equipment masses to answer: Which item weighs more than \(\dfrac{1}{4}\) kg but less than \(\dfrac{1}{2}\) kg?
questions.hint: Convert both fractions of a kilogram to grams: 1/4 kg = 250 g and 1/2 kg = 500 g. Then find the item between 250 g and 500 g.

keyPoints.note: Remember 1 kg = 1000 g, 1/2 kg = 500 g, and 1/4 kg = 250 g.

topics.title: Digital time: Represent and interpret digital time displays; connect analogue and digital

questions.stem: How do you write "3 o'clock" as a digital time?
questions.hint: For "o'clock" or "past" times, write the hour first, then a colon, then the two-digit minutes past the hour.

keyPoints.note: O'clock means 00 minutes past the hour.
Digital format is hour:minutes with two digits for minutes.

steps.explain: Visualise "3 o'clock" on an analogue clock face to see where the hour hand and minute hand point.

questions.stem: How do you write "quarter past 7" as a digital time?
questions.hint: For "o'clock" or "past" times, write the hour first, then a colon, then the two-digit minutes past the hour.

keyPoints.note: One quarter of 60 minutes is 15 minutes past 7.
Digital format is hour:minutes with two digits for minutes.

questions.stem: How do you write "25 past 8" as a digital time?
questions.hint: For "o'clock" or "past" times, write the hour first, then a colon, then the two-digit minutes past the hour.

keyPoints.note: 25 past 8 means the hour is 8 and 25 minutes have passed.
Digital format is hour:minutes with two digits for minutes.

questions.stem: How do you write "quarter to 10" as a digital time?
questions.hint: For "to" times, the digital hour is 1 less than the stated hour, and the minutes equal 60 minus the minutes to the hour.

keyPoints.note: Quarter to 10 is 15 minutes before 10:00, so the hour is still 9 and minutes = 60 - 15 = 45.
Digital format is hour:minutes with two digits for minutes.

steps.explain: Visualise "quarter to 10" on an analogue clock face to see where the hour hand and minute hand point.

questions.stem: How do you write "10 to 5" as a digital time?
questions.hint: For "to" times, the digital hour is 1 less than the stated hour, and the minutes equal 60 minus the minutes to the hour.

keyPoints.note: 10 to 5 is 10 minutes before 5:00, so the hour is still 4 and minutes = 60 - 10 = 50.
Digital format is hour:minutes with two digits for minutes.

questions.stem: How do you write "5 past 3" as a digital time?
questions.hint: For "o'clock" or "past" times, write the hour first, then a colon, then the two-digit minutes past the hour.

keyPoints.note: 5 past 3 means hour 3 and 05 minutes (always write two digits for minutes!).
Digital format is hour:minutes with two digits for minutes.

questions.stem: How do you write "half past 1" as a digital time?
questions.hint: For "o'clock" or "past" times, write the hour first, then a colon, then the two-digit minutes past the hour.

keyPoints.note: Half of 60 minutes is 30 minutes past 1.
Digital format is hour:minutes with two digits for minutes.

questions.stem: How do you write "20 to 8" as a digital time?
questions.hint: For "to" times, the digital hour is 1 less than the stated hour, and the minutes equal 60 minus the minutes to the hour.

keyPoints.note: 20 to 8 is 20 minutes before 8:00, so the hour is still 7 and minutes = 60 - 20 = 40.
Digital format is hour:minutes with two digits for minutes.

steps.explain: Visualise "20 to 8" on an analogue clock face to see where the hour hand and minute hand point.

questions.stem: How do you write the digital time \(8:30\) as an analogue time in words?
questions.hint: Since 30 minutes is 30 or less, read it as minutes PAST 8 (remember 15 = quarter past, 30 = half past, 00 = o'clock).

keyPoints.note: Numbers before the colon show the hour; numbers after show minutes past.
Use "past" up to 30 minutes and "to" the next hour after 30 minutes.

steps.explain: Read the hour before the colon (\(8\)) and the minutes after the colon (\(30\)).

questions.stem: How do you write the digital time \(7:15\) as an analogue time in words?
questions.hint: Since 15 minutes is 30 or less, read it as minutes PAST 7 (remember 15 = quarter past, 30 = half past, 00 = o'clock).

keyPoints.note: Numbers before the colon show the hour; numbers after show minutes past.

steps.explain: Read the hour before the colon (\(7\)) and the minutes after the colon (\(15\)).

questions.stem: How do you write the digital time \(6:45\) as an analogue time in words?
questions.hint: Since 45 minutes is past half past (30), subtract 45 from 60 to find how many minutes TO the next hour (7).

keyPoints.note: Numbers before the colon show the hour; numbers after show minutes past.
Use "past" up to 30 minutes and "to" the next hour after 30 minutes.

steps.explain: Read the hour before the colon (\(6\)) and the minutes after the colon (\(45\)).

steps.explain: Because \(45 > 30\), we express the time as minutes TO the next hour (\(6 + 1 = 7\)).

questions.stem: How do you write the digital time \(2:25\) as an analogue time in words?
questions.hint: Since 25 minutes is 30 or less, read it as minutes PAST 2 (remember 15 = quarter past, 30 = half past, 00 = o'clock).

keyPoints.note: Numbers before the colon show the hour; numbers after show minutes past.
Use "past" up to 30 minutes and "to" the next hour after 30 minutes.

steps.explain: Read the hour before the colon (\(2\)) and the minutes after the colon (\(25\)).

questions.stem: How do you write the digital time \(8:50\) as an analogue time in words?
questions.hint: Since 50 minutes is past half past (30), subtract 50 from 60 to find how many minutes TO the next hour (9).

keyPoints.note: Numbers before the colon show the hour; numbers after show minutes past.

steps.explain: Read the hour before the colon (\(8\)) and the minutes after the colon (\(50\)).

questions.hint: Since 20 minutes is 30 or less, read it as minutes PAST 2 (remember 15 = quarter past, 30 = half past, 00 = o'clock).

keyPoints.note: Numbers before the colon show the hour; numbers after show minutes past.

steps.explain: Read the hour before the colon (\(2\)) and the minutes after the colon (\(20\)).

questions.stem: How do you write the digital time \(4:40\) as an analogue time in words?
questions.hint: Since 40 minutes is past half past (30), subtract 40 from 60 to find how many minutes TO the next hour (5).

keyPoints.note: Numbers before the colon show the hour; numbers after show minutes past.
Use "past" up to 30 minutes and "to" the next hour after 30 minutes.

steps.explain: Read the hour before the colon (\(4\)) and the minutes after the colon (\(40\)).

questions.hint: Read the shorter hour hand first (it has passed the current hour, even if close to the next number!), then count by 5s and 1s for the longer minute hand.

keyPoints.note: Short hand = hour; long hand = exact minutes (each small tick = 1 minute).

steps.explain: Look at the shorter hour hand first. It sits between \(8\) and \(9\), which means the hour is still \(8\).

questions.stem: What digital time is shown on this analogue clock?
questions.hint: Read the shorter hour hand first (it has passed the current hour, even if close to the next number!), then count by 5s and 1s for the longer minute hand.

keyPoints.note: Short hand = hour; long hand = exact minutes (each small tick = 1 minute).

steps.explain: Look at the shorter hour hand first. It sits between \(7\) and \(8\), which means the hour is still \(7\).

questions.stem: What digital time is shown on this analogue clock?
questions.hint: Read the shorter hour hand first (it has passed the current hour, even if close to the next number!), then count by 5s and 1s for the longer minute hand.

keyPoints.note: Short hand = hour; long hand = exact minutes (each small tick = 1 minute).

steps.explain: Look at the shorter hour hand first. It sits between \(2\) and \(3\), which means the hour is still \(2\).

questions.stem: What digital time is shown on this analogue clock?
questions.hint: Read the shorter hour hand first (it has passed the current hour, even if close to the next number!), then count by 5s and 1s for the longer minute hand.

keyPoints.note: Short hand = hour; long hand = exact minutes (each small tick = 1 minute).

steps.explain: Look at the shorter hour hand first. It sits between \(4\) and \(5\), which means the hour is still \(4\).

questions.hint: Read the shorter hour hand first (it has passed the current hour, even if close to the next number!), then count by 5s and 1s for the longer minute hand.

keyPoints.note: Short hand = hour; long hand = exact minutes (each small tick = 1 minute).

steps.explain: Look at the shorter hour hand first. It sits between \(8\) and \(9\), which means the hour is still \(8\).

questions.stem: What digital time is shown on this analogue clock?
questions.hint: Read the shorter hour hand first (it has passed the current hour, even if close to the next number!), then count by 5s and 1s for the longer minute hand.

keyPoints.note: Short hand = hour; long hand = exact minutes (each small tick = 1 minute).

steps.explain: Look at the shorter hour hand first. It sits between \(6\) and \(7\), which means the hour is still \(6\).

questions.hint: Read the shorter hour hand first (it has passed the current hour, even if close to the next number!), then count by 5s and 1s for the longer minute hand.

keyPoints.note: Short hand = hour; long hand = exact minutes (each small tick = 1 minute).

questions.stem: What digital time is shown on this analogue clock?
questions.hint: Read the shorter hour hand first (it has passed the current hour, even if close to the next number!), then count by 5s and 1s for the longer minute hand.

keyPoints.note: Short hand = hour; long hand = exact minutes (each small tick = 1 minute).

steps.explain: Look at the shorter hour hand first. It sits between \(1\) and \(2\), which means the hour is still \(1\).
